title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
abstract: arXiv:2611.14413v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B with simulated round-to-nearest weight quantization (8, 6, 4 and 3 bits, fp16 reference), read from the logits of the letters A to D on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag (300 items each), 6 bits lose no accuracy against fp16 (they score +1.8 (+1.0 to +2.5) and +0.9 (+0.3 to +1.5) points higher, which we do not explain), and 8 bits change it by -0.7 (-1.1 to -0.3) and -0.4 (-0.7 to -0.2) points. At 4 bits the answer-slot skew rises from 0.15 to 0.53 (0.6B) and from 0.07 to 0.12 (1.7B); Gaussian noise at the same weight SNR gives 0.15 and 0.37 (two draws) and 0.19 (one draw), so the control is inconclusive on whether rounding adds slot

translated_title: 比特还是排列？在小型本地语言模型中将固定推理预算用于权重精度还是选项顺序平均
translated_abstract: 本地语言模型可以通过以更少的比特数存储权重来节省内存，也可以通过对少量选项重排序的结果取平均来降低对答案选项顺序的敏感性。我们探讨前者是否会使后者变差，以及在固定预算下哪种方式是更经济的花费方式。在Qwen3-0.6B和Qwen3-1.7B上使用模拟的就近取整权重量化（8、6、4和3比特，以fp16为参照），读取ARC-Easy、ARC-Challenge、MMLU和HellaSwag（各300题）上字母A到D的logits，结果显示：6比特相比fp16没有损失准确率（反而分别高出+1.8（+1.0到+2.5）和+0.9（+0.3到+1.5）分，这一点我们无法解释），而8比特使准确率变化-0.7（-1.1到-0.3）和-0.4（-0.7到-0.2）分。在4比特时，答案槽位偏斜从0.15升至0.53（0.6B模型），从0.07升至0.12（1.7B模型）；在相同权重信噪比下施加高斯噪声得到0.15和0.37（两次抽样）以及0.19（一次抽样），因此该对照实验对于取整是否增加了槽位（偏斜）尚无定论。
tldr: 本文量化了小型本地语言模型中权重量化精度对答案选项顺序偏差的影响，发现6比特量化不损失准确率而4比特量化会显著加剧答案槽位偏斜，并据此比较了固定推理预算下提升权重精度与选项顺序平均两种方案的性价比。
en_tdlr: This study quantifies how weight quantization precision affects answer-option-order bias in small local language models, finding that 6-bit quantization costs no accuracy while 4-bit quantization substantially increases answer-slot skew, and compares which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed inference budget: higher weight precision or option-order averaging.
